extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: The Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) is a reading comprehension dataset consisting of over 100,000 questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of English Wikipedia articles. The answer to every question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar (Stanford University); Jian Zhang (Stanford University); Konstantin Lopyrev (Stanford University); Percy Liang (Stanford University)
extraction.citeAs: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang. SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected in three stages: curating passages by sampling 536 articles from the top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles, extracting paragraphs, and employing crowdworkers via the Daemo platform (backed by Amazon Mechanical Turk) to ask and answer up to 5 questions per paragraph.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator; Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer. Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The top 10,000 articles of English Wikipedia, obtained using Project Nayuki's Wikipedia's internal PageRanks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions per paragraph by entering questions in a text field and highlighting the answer span. Workers were guided by examples, encouraged to use their own words, and restricted from copy-pasting. For development and test sets, additional workers selected the shortest answer span for the generated questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement was calculated to establish human performance. For development and test sets, multiple answers were collected and kept as ground truth.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 for training set, at least 3 for development and test sets
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Located in the United States or Canada
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions with span-based answers are more constrained than the more interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Reading comprehension; Training and evaluating expressive models
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: From each of these articles, we extracted individual paragraphs, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
